summary: The student/harness/session layer is a thin, heavily-commented wrapper around spawning a headless CLI and parsing its event stream. `src/cliStudent.ts` is the reference engine: it spawns `claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose` with `shell: true`, writes the prompt on stdin, consumes NDJSON line-by-line, accumulates per-message usage keyed by `message.id`, enforces a turn/token budget by tree-killing the child, runs a tick-counted idle watchdog, and settles on the child's `close` event. `src/harness.ts` (#298/#304) added a registry + a deliberately non-lowest-common-denominator `Harness` interface whose five booleans (`warmSessions`, `seedableSessions`, `cacheUsageSplit`, `toolAllowlist`, `budgetStop`) are declared per adapter and drive both warm/cold behaviour and usage fidelity. `src/claudeCodeHarness.ts` forwards verbatim into `runCliTask`; `src/openCodeHarness.ts` (#306) is the second adapter, with its own argv builder (`opencode run --format json --auto --dir … -m … -s … --fork <prompt>`, `shell: false`, prompt positional), its own NDJSON parser keyed on `part.type === 'step-finish'`, its own binary resolution, and no budget/idle machinery at all. `src/warmCliSession.ts` owns the seed-or-adopt-then-resume state machine; commit 6ffdbbc (#307) split `seedableSessions` out of `warmSessions` so an adopt-only harness learns its base id from `CliTaskResult.sessionId`. Every completed run appends one flat JSON row to `~/.claude-study-room/usage.jsonl` (`src/usageStore.ts`), tagged with `harness` and `fidelity` derived from capabilities so #301's $/AC comparison cannot silently pool unpriceable rows. Crucially, the board loop in `live.ts` calls `getHarness().run(...)` directly with **no** session flags and never with a harness id, so production students are cold single-shot spawns of `claude-code`; `WarmCliSession` is wired only into the Editor. Capacity/infra classification is three separate regexes over a free-text error message, and the plan-reset time is parsed out of the CLI's own English wording by a module that is not part of the `Harness` interface.
facts: claude argv is built at src/cliStudent.ts:302-306: `['-p','--output-format','stream-json','--verbose', ...perm, ...(model?['--model',model]:[]), ...toolList, ...session]`. Asserted byte-for-byte in test/cliStudent.test.ts:69-75.

Permission mapping, src/cliStudent.ts:283-285: `permissionMode === 'bypassPermissions'` (the default, src/cliStudent.ts:278) emits `['--dangerously-skip-permissions']`; ANY other value emits `['--permission-mode', <mode>]`. Test: test/cliStudent.test.ts:77-82 (`acceptEdits`).
Session flags, src/cliStudent.ts:288-292, emitted in this fixed order: `--session-id <id>`, then `--resume <id>`, then `--fork-session` (bare, no value). Tests: test/cliStudent.test.ts:99-116.

Tool allowlist, src/cliStudent.ts:302: `tools && tools.length ? ['--tools', ...tools] : []` — each tool name is a SEPARATE argv entry, never comma-joined (test/studentTools.test.ts:46-56); an empty/omitted list emits no flag at all, leaving the CLI default surface.

DEFAULT_STUDENT_TOOLS = ['Bash','Read','Edit','Write','Grep','Glob','PowerShell','WebFetch','WebSearch'] (src/cliStudent.ts:103-105), measured at -11,382 tokens/turn vs the full surface (29,553 → 18,171).

Spawn call: `spawnFn(claudeBin, args, { cwd, shell: true, windowsHide: true })` (src/cliStudent.ts:309); prompt goes over stdin (`child.stdin.write(prompt); child.stdin.end()`, src/cliStudent.ts:311-312). `claudeBin` defaults to the literal string 'claude' (src/cliStudent.ts:278).

There is NO effort/reasoning flag anywhere in the argv. `Effort = 'low'|'medium'|'high'|'xhigh'` exists (src/difficulty.ts:11, effortFor at src/difficulty.ts:77) but is only attached to the dashboard student card (src/live.ts:2047) and simulated in src/pool.ts:241 — it never reaches the CLI.

Stream parsing (src/cliStudent.ts:405-414): stdout is split on '\n' with a `pending` partial-line buffer; each non-empty trimmed line is JSON.parse'd inside try/catch (non-JSON noise is silently skipped, test/cliStudent.test.ts:199-205); a final unterminated line is flushed on close (src/cliStudent.ts:453).

Event handling (src/cliStudent.ts:347-403): `evt.type === 'result'` is stored as the authoritative result; otherwise `evt.message.content[]` blocks with `{type:'text'}` update `lastText`, and `evt.message.usage` {input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens} is stored in a Map keyed by `evt.message.id` (fallback `anon-${perMessage.size}`, src/cliStudent.ts:369).

Live usage semantics (src/cliStudent.ts:377-388): `outputTokens` is SUMMED across messages; `inputTokens`/`cacheRead`/`cacheCreate` take the LAST message's values (context, not a sum) because summing would double-count. Asserted in test/cliStudent.test.ts:164-174 (`[[10,500,100],[35,600,200]]`).

Final result parsing (src/cliStudent.ts:454-509): fields read are `result` (must be typeof string else reject), `is_error`, `subtype`, `session_id`, `usage.*`. `turns` in CliTaskResult is `perMessage.size`, NOT the CLI's `num_turns`. `total_cost_usd` and `num_turns` are NEVER read anywhere in src/ (grep: only test/cliStudent.test.ts:47).

parseUsage (src/cliStudent.ts:235-243) maps snake_case → camelCase with 0 defaults: input_tokens→inputTokens, output_tokens→outputTokens, cache_read_input_tokens→cacheReadInputTokens, cache_creation_input_tokens→cacheCreationInputTokens.

Failure messages, verbatim: `claude -p (${code}) returned no JSON result: ${tail}` where tail = last 500 chars of stderr||stdout or '(no output)' (src/cliStudent.ts:495-496); `claude -p error (${parsed.subtype ?? code}): ${String(parsed.result).slice(-500)}` (src/cliStudent.ts:500).

Legacy fallback (src/cliStudent.ts:458-460): if no `type:'result'` event was seen, the whole stdout is JSON.parse'd as a single blob — covers a CLI build that ignores `--output-format stream-json` (test/cliStudent.test.ts:209-214).

Budget: `overBudget(turns, tokens, budget)` at src/cliStudent.ts:161-166 returns 'maxTurns' if `budget.maxTurns && turns >= budget.maxTurns`, else 'maxTokens' if `budget.maxTokens && tokens >= budget.maxTokens`; 0/undefined means OFF, never 'stop immediately'.

Budget token metric: `billedTokens()` (src/cliStudent.ts:147-151) sums `in + cRead + cCreate` across ALL distinct messages — a different accumulation from the live onUsage report, which takes the last message's input.

Budget trip path (src/cliStudent.ts:394-402): after reporting usage, sets `stopped`, calls `onBudgetStop({turns: perMessage.size, tokens, limit})`, then `treeKill(child)`; a guard at src/cliStudent.ts:351 drops every event still in the pipe so the reported turn count never exceeds the cap.

Budget stop RESOLVES, never rejects (src/cliStudent.ts:473-492): text = `[stopped by the ${stopped} budget after ${n} turns — this is PARTIAL work, not a finished task]`, usage totals (output summed, input/cache = last message), `sessionId: parsed?.session_id ?? opts.sessionId ?? ''`, `stoppedBy: 'budget'` — so the caller's commit→push→PR path still banks the worktree edits.

DEFAULT_STUDENT_BUDGET is `{}` — the cap is OFF by default (src/config.ts:169). Reverted because with implement capped at 70 turns / 8M tokens, tokens per MERGED PR went 9.5M → 20.5M; the cap fired on maxTokens every time at 35-59 turns, with real context/turn of 160-230k vs the 84k it was sized against (src/config.ts:148-168).

Idle watchdog: IDLE_TICK_MS = 60_000 (src/cliStudent.ts:132), DEFAULT_IDLE_TICKS = 20 (src/cliStudent.ts:144), counted in TICKS not wall-clock so a sleeping machine cannot accrue idleness; timer is `unref()`d (src/cliStudent.ts:435). Rejection text: `claude -p produced no output for ${n} consecutive minute(s) — killed as stalled. Last message: ${lastText.slice(0,300)}` (src/cliStudent.ts:448-450).
Capacity classifier (src/cliStudent.ts:182-185): `/session limit|rate limit|usage limit|quota|too many requests|429|overloaded|capacity|try again later|resets? (at|in|\d)/i`.

OpenCode capacity classifier (src/openCodeHarness.ts:152-156) = claude's regex OR `/rate_limit_exceeded|insufficient_quota|context length|model is loading|no such model|connection refused|ECONNREFUSED/i`.

Infra classifier (src/infraFailure.ts:30-33): `/returned no JSON result|segmentation fault|bun has crashed|^\s*panic\(|oh no: bun|spawn \S+ ENOENT|ETXTBSY/im`. It is NOT part of the Harness interface — live.ts:2128 calls the module function directly, so any harness must phrase its crash as 'returned no JSON result' to be forgiven.

Infra backoff (src/infraFailure.ts:48-59): INFRA_PAUSE_AFTER=3 consecutive, INFRA_PAUSE_BASE_MS=2min doubling per extra failure, INFRA_PAUSE_MAX_MS=15min. Streak reset on any successful run (src/live.ts:2117).

Capacity reset parsing (src/capacityReset.ts:24): `/resets?\s+(\d{1,2})(?::(\d{2}))?\s*(am|pm)\b(?:\s*\(([^)]+)\))?/i`; MAX_RESET_WAIT_MS = 25h (src/capacityReset.ts:35), RESET_MARGIN_MS = 60s (src/capacityReset.ts:45); returns null on unknown timezone / implausible wait so the caller falls back to a flat backoff.

Error routing in live.ts:2122-2130: capacity checked FIRST (`getHarness().isCapacityError(msg)` → noteCapacityBlocked → parseCapacityReset → pauseCapacity), infra checked only if not capacity. Both add the action key to `capacityFailed` so the watchdog forgives instead of condemning the item.

Harness interface (src/harness.ts:79-93): `{ readonly id: string; readonly capabilities: HarnessCapabilities; run(prompt, opts): Promise<CliTaskResult>; killAll(): void; isCapacityError(message: string): boolean }` — five members, nothing else.
HarnessCapabilities (src/harness.ts:37-66): warmSessions, seedableSessions, cacheUsageSplit, toolAllowlist, budgetStop — all plain booleans.

`export type HarnessRunOptions = RunCliTaskOptions` (src/harness.ts:76) — the seam is a type ALIAS, so it leaks Claude-specific `claudeBin`, node-specific `spawnFn: typeof spawn`, `setIntervalFn`, `idleTicks`, `onIdleKill`, `budget`, `onBudgetStop`, `tools: string[]`, `permissionMode: string` (src/cliStudent.ts:187-231). The file names this a 'Known wart for #299'.
`fidelityFor(harness)` (src/harness.ts:105-107) = `capabilities.cacheUsageSplit ? 'exact' : 'partial'` — fidelity is derived, never passed, so an adapter cannot claim 'exact' by omission.

Registry (src/harness.ts:112-166): `registerHarness` returns the displaced harness; `getHarness(id = 'claude-code')` THROWS `unknown harness "x" — registered: …` rather than falling back (test/harness.test.ts:67-70); `killAllHarnesses()` sweeps every registration and swallows individual throws (test/harness.test.ts:106-114); `clearHarnesses()` is the test seam.

src/harnesses.ts:19-23 registers claudeCodeHarness then openCodeHarness at import time; the file exists solely to keep the import graph a DAG and consumers are told to import getHarness from here, never from harness.js.

CLAUDE_CODE_CAPABILITIES = all five true (src/claudeCodeHarness.ts:31-37). OPENCODE_CAPABILITIES = { warmSessions: true, seedableSessions: false, cacheUsageSplit: true, toolAllowlist: false, budgetStop: false } (src/openCodeHarness.ts:87-93).

OpenCode argv (src/openCodeHarness.ts:184-200): `['run','--format','json', ...(bypass?['--auto']:[]), '--dir', cwd, ...(model?['-m',model]:[]), ...(resume?['-s',resume]:[]), ...(resume && forkSession?['--fork']:[]), prompt]` — prompt is the LAST POSITIONAL arg. `opts.sessionId` is deliberately dropped (server-assigned ids only). Spawned with `{ cwd, shell: false, windowsHide: true }` (src/openCodeHarness.ts:254) precisely so a model-authored prompt containing & | % is not shell-parsed.

OpenCode NDJSON parse (src/openCodeHarness.ts:120-145): only lines starting with '{'; `sessionId ||= ev.part?.sessionID ?? ev.sessionID`; `part.type === 'text'` appends `part.text`; `part.type === 'step-finish'` sets sawResult, increments turns, and folds `part.tokens`.

addStepTokens (src/openCodeHarness.ts:110-117): inputTokens += tokens.input; outputTokens += tokens.output + tokens.reasoning (reasoning is billed as output on purpose); cacheReadInputTokens += tokens.cache.read; cacheCreationInputTokens += tokens.cache.write. Verified against a real run where input 6472 + output 2 + cache.read 5 == total 6479 (test/openCodeHarness.test.ts:17-52).

OpenCode failure: rejects `opencode: no JSON result (exit ${code})${detail}` with detail = first 400 chars of stderr||stdout when no step-finish was seen (src/openCodeHarness.ts:281-284) — deliberately phrased to match isInfraFailure's 'returned no JSON result'… but note it says 'no JSON result', which DOES match the regex substring.

OpenCode binary resolution (src/openCodeHarness.ts:228-242): `OPENCODE_BIN` env wins; else `<APPDATA>/npm/node_modules/opencode-ai/bin/opencode.exe` or `$HOME/AppData/Roaming/npm/...` on win32, `~/.local/bin | /usr/local/lib | /opt/homebrew/lib` + `/node_modules/opencode-ai/bin/opencode` elsewhere; else `resolveCliBin('opencode')`. Quotes are stripped (src/openCodeHarness.ts:204-206) because shell:false makes a quoted path a literal filename. `opts.claudeBin` is explicitly NOT consulted.

claudeBin.ts: `resolveClaudeBin(configured, env, home)` (src/claudeBin.ts:84-106) — explicit path returned shell-quoted; bare name found on PATH returned unchanged; else probes fallbackDirs (win32: `~/.local/bin`, `~/.claude/local`, `%APPDATA%/npm`, `%ProgramFiles%/nodejs`; posix: `~/.local/bin`, `~/.claude/local`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`) against PATHEXT (src/claudeBin.ts:23-49); memoized; NO `--version` spawn. `export const resolveCliBin = resolveClaudeBin` (src/claudeBin.ts:115) is the #299 generalisation.

WarmCliSession state (src/warmCliSession.ts:40-69): `sessionId` (randomUUID default), `harness` (getHarness() default), private `baseSeeded`, `adoptedSessionId`, `_state: 'idle-warm'|'busy'`, `warnedCold`. A caller-supplied id on a NON-seedable harness is treated as a real server id and pre-adopted (src/warmCliSession.ts:63-65).

WarmCliSession.run branching (src/warmCliSession.ts:136-143): `!supportsWarm` → NO session flags + one-time `log.warn('harness "X" has no warm sessions — slot <id> runs cold, paying repo ramp-up on every task')`; `baseId` exists → `{resume: base, forkSession: true}`; no base + canSeed → `{sessionId}`; no base + adopt-only → bare run, then `adoptedSessionId = result.sessionId` on success only (src/warmCliSession.ts:156-158).

`baseId` (src/warmCliSession.ts:89-93) replaced the boolean `baseSeeded` as source of truth in 6ffdbbc, because 'seeded' and 'seeded AND we know its name' are different states; `isWarm` derives from it so an unseeded slot never counts toward warm capacity. `wipeContext()` is a documented no-op (src/warmCliSession.ts:171-173) — the fork IS the wipe.

Commit 6ffdbbc (2026-09-11, 'feat(harness): let a warm slot adopt a server-assigned session id', Refs #307) touched README.md, claudeCodeHarness.ts, harness.ts, openCodeHarness.ts, warmCliSession.ts, test/adoptSession.test.ts (+130 new), harness.test.ts, openCodeHarness.test.ts. Live proof in the message: run1 input=2329 cacheRead=4151; run2 input=2645 cacheRead=4151; run3 input=8 cacheRead=6788, vs a cold first run at input=6475/12.8s. 851 tests pass.
usage.jsonl path: `join(homedir(), '.claude-study-room', 'usage.jsonl')` (src/usageStore.ts:103-105), engine-wide (NOT per-repo) so $/AC can be queried across boards with one read.

UsageRecord fields (src/usageStore.ts:81-96), in order: ts (ISO), repo, item, role, tier, model|null, harness, fidelity, inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadInputTokens, cacheCreationInputTokens, turns|null, stoppedBy:'budget'|null. Example row in README.md:185-191.

UsageFidelity = 'exact' | 'partial' | 'missing' (src/usageStore.ts:49-57). toUsageRecord defaults `fidelity` to `ctx.fidelity ?? (usage ? 'exact' : 'missing')` (src/usageStore.ts:124) — a harness that returns a zeroed-but-present usage object records 'exact' zeros, not 'missing'.
appendUsage NEVER throws (src/usageStore.ts:148-155): mkdirSync recursive + appendFileSync, errors logged via log.warn and swallowed; synchronous on purpose.

live.ts recordUsage (src/live.ts:2072-2099) writes BOTH the in-memory attribution cell (tasks, tokens, cost via taskCost, cacheReadTokens, cacheInputTokens) and the durable row, deriving `harness: getHarness().id` and `fidelity: fidelityFor(harness)` then spreading `...ctx` AFTER them (src/live.ts:2096-2098).

Board dispatch call sites all use `getHarness().run(...)` with NO session flags: implement src/live.ts:2171-2183 (passes onUsage, cwd, model: cfg.pool[tier].model, permissionMode, claudeBin, tools, onIdleKill, budget: cfg.studentBudget?.implement, onBudgetStop); review src/live.ts:2298-2307 (no budget); fix/rewrite src/live.ts:2445-2455 (no budget); resolve src/live.ts:2566; triage src/live.ts:1899; splitRunner src/splitRunner.ts:79 (only cwd + model).

`getHarness()` is NEVER called with an argument in src/ (grep: the only occurrence with a parameter is the definition at src/harness.ts:137). There is no `harness` key in StudyRoomConfig (src/config.ts:94-146). #300 (per-task harness routing from labels) is unimplemented and labelled `blocked`.

pricing.ts: PRICE_PER_MILLION = haiku{input 1, output 5}, sonnet{3,15}, opus{5,25} (src/pricing.ts:20-24); CACHE_WRITE_MULT 1.25, CACHE_READ_MULT 0.1 (src/pricing.ts:26-27); taskCost is documented as an estimated EQUIVALENT API cost, never billed on a subscription (src/pricing.ts:29-32).

Subscription proxies: `tokensProcessed = input + output + cacheRead` (src/pricing.ts:53-55); `cacheHitPct = round(cacheRead / (input + cacheRead + cacheCreate) * 100)` (src/pricing.ts:62-65). These are the ONLY plan-usage meters in the codebase — nothing queries a provider for quota left.

tierFallback.effectiveTier (src/tierFallback.ts:13-24): a tier with maxWarm 0 is disabled; fallback searches UPWARD in TIERS (haiku<sonnet<opus) first, then downward, returning the original tier when nothing is enabled.

ManagedProcess (src/managedProcess.ts) is the dashboard-side wrapper for the engine + editor children: bounded ring (default 800 lines, src/managedProcess.ts:51), optional tee to a log file with 2-generation rotation at 5 MiB (src/managedProcess.ts:53, 119-126), `start` returns false if already running, `stop()` = taskkill /T /F on win32 else SIGTERM, `kill()` = taskkill /T /F else SIGKILL and never throws (src/managedProcess.ts:158-182).
Tree-kill is implemented THREE times, identically: src/cliStudent.ts:255-262, src/openCodeHarness.ts:160-167, src/managedProcess.ts:180-182 — all `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F` on win32 else a signal.

`activeChildren`/`active` are module-level Sets (src/cliStudent.ts:249, src/openCodeHarness.ts:158); `killAllStudents()`/`killAllOpenCode()` reap everything. There is no per-run cancel handle and no AbortSignal anywhere in the run options.

Test doubles: every test fakes `spawnFn` as an EventEmitter with {stdin:{write,end}, stdout, stderr} (test/cliStudent.test.ts:17-38, test/harness.test.ts:20-39, test/openCodeHarness.test.ts:23-41); WarmCliSession tests inject `runFn` instead (test/adoptSession.test.ts:9-19). test/harness.test.ts:87-101 asserts argv/bin/stdin are byte-identical direct vs via the harness.

Issue #300 'Route harness per task from the issue's labels' (OPEN, blocked): wants tierForDifficulty() → {harness, model}, config-driven and inert by default, harness id visible on the pool grid and in the usage store, and a REFUSAL at dispatch when declared capabilities cannot support the role — never a silent degrade. Cites Omnigent's `executor: {harness, model, reasoning_effort, auth}` as the schema to copy.

Issue #301 'Measure $/AC of the second-harness lane against the $2.72 baseline' (OPEN, blocked): baseline $2.72 equivalent / 2.97M tokens per acceptance criterion, IQR $1.64-$3.70, over 74 merged dungeonworks issues (2026-08-31). Requires AC-count denominator (diff-based rejected despite rho=0.79 vs 0.69 because it rewards verbosity), partial-fidelity rows reported separately, and subscription vs metered spend as DISTINCT meters never summed.

Issue #307 (OPEN) is the one 6ffdbbc implements: adopt-then-resume, capability split, `-s <adopted id> --fork` on second+ tasks, first-run failure must not poison the slot, isWarm false until a base genuinely exists, and a live run proving a higher cache.read on task 2.

Transcript reconstruction still exists as ad-hoc scripts with a HARDCODED absolute path: `const PROJECTS = 'C:\\Users\\pegan\\.claude\\projects'` at audit-correlate.ts:12 and card-dryrun.ts:92, walking `*.jsonl` files. usageStore.ts:12-24 calls this an 'accident' that ends the moment a second harness runs a task.

reusable.what: The capability-declaring Harness interface + registry (registerHarness / getHarness / harnessIds / killAllHarnesses / clearHarnesses) and fidelityFor().
reusable.why_keep: The *shape* of the idea is right and hard-won: capabilities declared not inferred, unknown id throws rather than falls back (so a config typo cannot run the control while claiming the experiment), fidelity DERIVED from a capability so an adapter cannot over-claim by omission, and shutdown sweeps the whole registry past a thrower. Port the design; widen the fields.
reusable.coupling: Imports only ./cliStudent.js types and ./usageStore.js UsageFidelity. The only real coupling is `HarnessRunOptions = RunCliTaskOptions`, which drags in claudeBin + node's spawn type. Trivial to lift once that alias is replaced by a real struct.

reusable.what: runCliTask: NDJSON line reassembly across chunk boundaries, per-message-id usage dedup, tick-counted idle watchdog, budget tree-kill that RESOLVES with banked partial work, single-blob fallback parse.
reusable.why_keep: Every one of these exists because of a documented production failure (a 12-hour hung student, a double-counted usage sum, an unbanked cap that wiped a worktree). The per-message-id dedup and the 'output sums, input/cache take the newest' rule are non-obvious and correct. The sleep-safe tick watchdog is the single best idea in the file — a setTimeout would massacre every student on lid-open.
reusable.coupling: Self-contained except node:child_process. No SDK, no config import. Directly liftable as a 'stream-json CLI runner' utility; the claude-specific parts are only the argv builder and the two error strings.

reusable.what: The seed-or-adopt-then-resume slot state machine: baseId as the source of truth, adopt-on-success-only, cold degradation logged once per slot.
reusable.why_keep: #307's lesson generalises to every future adapter: 'can hold a warm base' and 'the caller may name it' are two different questions, and conflating them costs a whole lane its warm start (the biggest measured cost lever: 9.5M → 20.5M tokens/merged PR when ramp-up is paid twice). Codex has the same property — rollout ids are locally assigned, not caller-chosen.
reusable.coupling: Imports getHarness (default harness) and log. Single-flight busy guard is built in. Currently only used by editor.ts:365 — lifting it costs nothing.

reusable.what: Append-only usage.jsonl with harness + fidelity on every row, never-throws write, and a pure toUsageRecord() worth unit-testing.
reusable.why_keep: This is the ONLY durable cross-harness spend record and the stated prerequisite for #301. The fidelity tri-state ('exact'/'partial'/'missing', with missing still counted in the denominator so an absent row cannot bias the average down) is the right answer to comparing providers that report different token shapes.
reusable.coupling: Imports Role (taskmap), Tier (pricing), CliUsage (cliStudent), log. The Role/Tier coupling is the only thing that would need generalising; the file is otherwise pure fs.

reusable.what: parseCapacityReset(message, now) — pulls 'resets 4:40am (America/New_York)' out of an error string into an absolute wake time, with a 25h sanity ceiling, a 60s margin, and Intl-based wall-clock diffing that sidesteps DST arithmetic.
reusable.why_keep: Pure over (message, now), fully unit-testable without an outage, and it removed a measured 126-dispatch retry-into-a-wall failure. The DEGRADE-TO-FLAT-BACKOFF-ON-DOUBT policy is exactly right.
reusable.coupling: Zero imports. Completely liftable. Its only weakness is that it is Claude-wording-specific and not reachable through the Harness interface.

reusable.what: isInfraFailure() + infraPauseMs() escalating backoff (3 consecutive → 2min doubling → 15min cap).
reusable.why_keep: Encodes the insight that a CRASH is worse than an outage because it is FREE — 95 segfaults burned the wedge ladder ~100x faster than designed and quarantined 22 healthy issues. Any v2 with a give-up ladder needs this distinction.
reusable.coupling: Zero imports. Liftable as-is. Should become a Harness member rather than a module-level regex.

reusable.what: resolveCliBin: PATH-then-known-install-locations probing with PATHEXT, memoized, filesystem-only (no --version spawn), shell-quoting for shell:true callers.
reusable.why_keep: Solves the real launch-context bug (a Scheduled Task / GUI shortcut carries a thinner PATH than the shell the config was written in). Already generalised past 'claude' in #299.
reusable.coupling: node:fs/os/path only. The `shellSafe` quoting is a shell:true artifact that openCodeHarness has to undo (unquoted()) — v2 should return {path, needsShell} instead.

reusable.what: Long-lived child wrapper: bounded log ring + tee to a rotating file, start/stop/kill with tree-kill, never-throw persist, 'error' listener so a spawn ENOENT cannot kill the parent.
reusable.why_keep: Solves 'a run you cannot read after it fails is a run you cannot fix' — which is precisely the gap for per-run transcript capture. The ring+file tee pattern is the obvious base for a v2 transcript sink.

reusable.what: Six cases covering adopt-then-resume, first-run-failure-does-not-poison, empty-id-is-not-a-base, persisted-id-is-resumed, claude seed path unchanged, no-warm-support cold path.
reusable.why_keep: This is the executable spec for the session state machine and it transfers verbatim to any new adapter. The `recorder(sessionIds[])` helper (adoptSession.test.ts:9-19) is the cheapest possible harness double.
reusable.coupling: Imports openCodeHarness/claudeCodeHarness only to borrow capability shapes; `harnessWith(over)` spreads a real harness. Would work against any two adapters.

reusable.what: makeSpawn() fake child + stubHarness() + the 'byte-identical argv' regression test (lines 87-101).
reusable.why_keep: The byte-identical-argv assertion is the technique that makes 'add a seam, change no behaviour' verifiable rather than asserted. Reuse it for every refactor of the argv builder.
reusable.coupling: None beyond node:test and the src modules under test.

pain_points.issue: The board loop never uses warm sessions — every production student is a COLD spawn, which contradicts the entire premise in CLAUDE.md.
pain_points.evidence: All six dispatch sites call `getHarness().run(...)` with no sessionId/resume/forkSession (live.ts:1899, 2171, 2298, 2445, 2566; splitRunner.ts:79). `WarmCliSession` appears in src/ only at editor.ts:5 and editor.ts:365. Protector has an `attach` hook for the real warm session (protector.ts:143-148, 179) but `new Protector({...})` at live.ts:206-211 passes no second argument, so `w.session` is always undefined.

pain_points.issue: `HarnessRunOptions` is a type alias of the Claude CLI's own options struct, so the 'seam' is not a seam — it exports claudeBin, node's spawn, setIntervalFn, idleTicks, budget and a Claude-shaped tool list to every adapter.
pain_points.evidence: src/harness.ts:76 `export type HarnessRunOptions = RunCliTaskOptions;` with the comment at src/harness.ts:70-75 admitting 'Known wart for #299: claudeBin names one specific binary.' openCodeHarness.ts:210-216 then has to document why it ignores `opts.claudeBin`, and silently ignores idleTicks/budget/setIntervalFn/onIdleKill/onBudgetStop with no capability flag covering them.

pain_points.issue: The OpenCode adapter has no idle watchdog and no budget enforcement, so the two guards that exist because of real 12-hour hangs and runaway sessions protect only the Claude lane.
pain_points.evidence: src/openCodeHarness.ts:253-293 wires only stdout/stderr/error/close — there is no interval, no `stopped` flag, no kill-on-silence. `budgetStop: false` (src/openCodeHarness.ts:92) declares the budget gap, but nothing declares the missing liveness watchdog, and `opts.idleTicks`/`opts.onIdleKill` are accepted by the type and dropped.

pain_points.issue: onUsage re-parses the ENTIRE accumulated stdout on every data chunk — O(n²) in stream length, on a lane whose measured floor is 6,472 input tokens of preamble.
pain_points.evidence: src/openCodeHarness.ts:262-268: `stdout += String(d); if (opts.onUsage) { const { usage } = parseOpenCodeStream(stdout); opts.onUsage(usage); }` — parseOpenCodeStream splits and JSON.parses every line seen so far, each time. cliStudent.ts:405-414 does it correctly with an incremental `pending` buffer.

pain_points.issue: Harness cannot report quota/usage-left at all. The only capacity signal in the system is a regex over an error message AFTER a run has already failed.
pain_points.evidence: The interface (src/harness.ts:79-93) has no quota/limits member. isCapacityError takes a string and returns a boolean — no reset time, no retry-after, no remaining budget. The reset time is recovered by a separate module (src/capacityReset.ts:80) that regexes Claude's English wording and is called from live.ts:611, not through the harness. Plan headroom is only ever proxied post-hoc by tokensProcessed/cacheHitPct (src/pricing.ts:53-65).

pain_points.issue: No transcript capture per run. The only thing that survives a run is the final `text` plus four token counts; the richest diagnostic the parser already holds is thrown away.
pain_points.evidence: `lastText` is maintained at src/cliStudent.ts:356-365 but used ONLY in the stall rejection message (src/cliStudent.ts:447). `stdout` is accumulated in full at src/cliStudent.ts:416 and then used only for the legacy-blob fallback (src/cliStudent.ts:459) and a 500-char error tail (src/cliStudent.ts:495). CliTaskResult (src/cliStudent.ts:27-36) has no transcript/events/log field. The workaround is walking `~/.claude/projects` with a hardcoded path (audit-correlate.ts:12, card-dryrun.ts:92) — exactly the 'accident' usageStore.ts:12-24 says ends with a second harness.

pain_points.issue: Infra-failure classification is a free module, not a Harness member, so a new adapter must phrase its crash message to match Claude's wording to be forgiven instead of condemning the item.
pain_points.evidence: src/infraFailure.ts:31 regexes the literal `returned no JSON result`; live.ts:2129 calls `isInfraFailure(msg)` directly rather than `getHarness().isInfraFailure(msg)`. openCodeHarness.ts:283 emits `opencode: no JSON result (exit N)` and its comment (src/openCodeHarness.ts:278-280) explicitly says it is phrased that way 'so the infra/capacity classifiers upstream read this failure identically' — a string coupling across two files with no test binding them.

pain_points.issue: taskCost() prices any harness's tokens at Anthropic tier prices, so a local Ollama run through OpenCode is billed as if it were Opus — the exact error #301 forbids.
pain_points.evidence: src/pricing.ts:33-42 takes only (tier, usage); there is no provider/meter dimension. live.ts:2088 does `cell.cost += taskCost(tier, u)` regardless of which harness ran. Issue #301's AC requires 'Subscription-backed and metered spend are reported as distinct meters, never summed into one number' — nothing implements that.

pain_points.issue: There is no way to select a harness. No config key, no CLI flag, no per-task routing — the second adapter is registered but unreachable.
pain_points.evidence: StudyRoomConfig (src/config.ts:94-146) has claudeBin/permissionMode/studentTools/studentBudget but no `harness`. `getHarness()` is never called with an id anywhere in src/. harnesses.ts:20-22 says 'Registered, not routed. Nothing reaches OpenCode until a config names it (#300)'. #300 is OPEN and labelled `blocked`.

pain_points.issue: No per-run cancellation. killAll() is the only stop, and it kills every in-flight student on that harness.
pain_points.evidence: Harness.killAll() (src/harness.ts:88) plus module-level Sets at src/cliStudent.ts:249 and src/openCodeHarness.ts:158. `run()` returns a bare Promise with no handle and no AbortSignal in RunCliTaskOptions (src/cliStudent.ts:187-231). Budget stop works only because the kill happens from INSIDE the same closure (src/cliStudent.ts:402).

pain_points.issue: `shell: true` for the claude spawn is a live injection surface that the sibling adapter deliberately refuses, and it forces path-quoting logic that then has to be undone.
pain_points.evidence: src/cliStudent.ts:309 `{ cwd, shell: true, ... }` (justified at src/cliStudent.ts:281-282 only because 'nothing dynamic crosses the shell' — true today, but `--model`, `--tools` entries and `--resume` values all reach argv). openCodeHarness.ts:179-183 spawns with shell:false for exactly the opposite reason, and openCodeHarness.ts:204-206 has to strip the quotes shellSafe() added (src/claudeBin.ts:66-68).

pain_points.issue: Two different token accumulations exist for the same run, and 'exact' fidelity can be recorded for a run that reported zeros.
pain_points.evidence: billedTokens() sums per-message input across messages (src/cliStudent.ts:147-151, used for the budget) while onUsage takes the LAST message's input (src/cliStudent.ts:379-388, used for the dashboard) — the same run reports two different input figures depending on who asks. Separately, toUsageRecord defaults to 'exact' whenever `usage` is a non-null object (src/usageStore.ts:124), so a harness returning all-zero usage writes an 'exact' zero row into the $/AC denominator.

pain_points.issue: Turn counting is inferred from distinct assistant message ids rather than read from the CLI's own `num_turns`, and messages without an id collapse into synthetic keys.
pain_points.evidence: src/cliStudent.ts:369 `const id = typeof msg?.id === 'string' ? msg.id : \`anon-${perMessage.size}\`` — an id-less message gets a key derived from the CURRENT map size, so two id-less messages arriving when the map is the same size overwrite each other. `num_turns` is never read (grep shows zero hits in src/). Turn count is the multiplier in the documented quadratic cost model (src/usageStore.ts:66-69).

pain_points.issue: No preflight/version/health member — an unresolvable or broken binary is discovered only by a failed student run, and claudeBin.ts deliberately refuses to answer the question.
pain_points.evidence: src/claudeBin.ts:17-20: 'Resolution is filesystem-only — no --version spawn — because loadConfig() runs on every 20s heartbeat… Whether the file is a WORKING CLI is still the preflight's question to answer.' The Harness interface (src/harness.ts:79-93) has no such member, so the preflight lives outside it and knows only about `claude`.

v2_implications: KEEP the anti-lowest-common-denominator stance, verbatim. src/harness.ts:11-29 is the most important design note in the layer: Omnigent normalises Claude Code/Codex/Cursor to an interface that hides harness-specific flags, and doing that here would erase `--session-id` / `--resume --fork-session`, which is the entire reason Study Room beats claude-queue-runner. v2 must keep capabilities DECLARED and inspectable, and must keep the rule that a caller adapts visibly rather than emitting a flag into the dark.

DROP `export type HarnessRunOptions = RunCliTaskOptions` (src/harness.ts:76). It is the single biggest blocker to a Codex adapter: it forces every adapter to accept `claudeBin`, node's `spawnFn`, `setIntervalFn`, `idleTicks`, `onIdleKill`, `budget`, `onBudgetStop` and a Claude-named `tools` list, most of which only cliStudent.ts implements. Replace with a real struct (below) plus a typed per-harness `extra` escape hatch.

ADD a per-harness binary/auth block to config. Today `cfg.claudeBin` is the only bin knob (src/config.ts:197) and OpenCode reads `process.env.OPENCODE_BIN` directly (src/openCodeHarness.ts:229) — an undocumented env convention. #300 already names the target schema: Omnigent's `executor: {harness, model, reasoning_effort, auth}`. `auth` and `reasoning_effort` currently have NO representation anywhere in the run path.

ADD reasoning effort to the run options. `Effort = 'low'|'medium'|'high'|'xhigh'` is computed (src/difficulty.ts:77) and displayed (src/live.ts:2047) but never sent. Codex's `-c model_reasoning_effort=...` and Claude's own effort control are both real levers, and CLAUDE.md's optimization toggle claims to derive `(model, effort, fast_mode, warm_count)` per task — half of that is currently fiction.

CHANGE permissionMode from a free string to a typed sandbox/approval enum. src/cliStudent.ts:283-285 treats exactly one value ('bypassPermissions') specially and passes everything else through to `--permission-mode`; openCodeHarness.ts:185 reduces the same string to a boolean `--auto`. Codex needs `--full-auto` / `--sandbox <mode>` / `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`, which do not map onto either. Make it `{ approval: 'never'|'on-request'|'on-failure', sandbox: 'none'|'workspace-write'|'read-only' }` and let each adapter project it.

CHANGE isCapacityError(string): boolean into a structured classifier that returns the reason AND the wake time. Fold src/capacityReset.ts:80 into the harness so a Codex adapter can supply its own reset wording or an HTTP Retry-After, and fold src/infraFailure.ts:30 in too — live.ts:2129 currently calls that module function directly, so any new adapter must literally emit the substring 'no JSON result' to be forgiven instead of condemning a healthy issue.

ADD per-provider quota reporting as a first-class, OPTIONAL member. Nothing in the system can answer 'how much plan is left' — the only signal is a regex over a failure that already happened (src/cliStudent.ts:182) plus post-hoc volume proxies (src/pricing.ts:53-65). A `quota()` returning `{ kind: 'subscription'|'metered'|'local'|'unknown', usedPct?, resetsAt?, retryAfterMs? }` is what lets the Protector schedule against headroom instead of discovering the wall, and it is also what #301's AC 'subscription-backed and metered spend reported as distinct meters' needs to be implementable at all. The `kind` field alone fixes src/pricing.ts:33, which currently prices a local Ollama run at Opus rates.

ADD transcript capture to the run contract. Today the only durable per-run artifact is four token counts plus final text (src/cliStudent.ts:27-36), and the richer analysis (cost_extract/comparator/ratio, audit-correlate.ts:12, card-dryrun.ts:92) works only by walking `~/.claude/projects` at a HARDCODED absolute path. usageStore.ts:12-24 already declares that accident dead on arrival for harness #2. v2 should have the harness write its own NDJSON transcript to a caller-supplied sink and return the path on the result — the raw stdout is already buffered in full (src/cliStudent.ts:416), so this is nearly free.

ADD budget enforcement as a GENERIC wrapper rather than a per-adapter capability. `budgetStop: false` on OpenCode (src/openCodeHarness.ts:92) is honest but unnecessary: the budget only needs (a) a usage signal, which OpenCode has via step-finish, and (b) a kill, which openCodeHarness.treeKill already implements. A shared runner that wraps any adapter's event stream could enforce StudentBudget and the idle watchdog uniformly — which would also close the gap that the OpenCode lane has NO liveness watchdog despite the 12-hour hang that justified it (src/cliStudent.ts:107-131).

KEEP budget-stop's resolve-don't-reject asymmetry and its exact reasoning (src/cliStudent.ts:465-491): a rejection skips commitAndPush, and the next dispatch force-removes the worktree and `branch -D`s it, so unbanked work is destroyed and the whole session is paid again. Any v2 stop/cancel path must bank first.

KEEP the tick-counted watchdog over any wall-clock timer (src/cliStudent.ts:120-131). This machine sleeps; a setTimeout fires already-expired on wake and would kill every in-flight student on lid-open. One healthy session showed a 238-minute gap followed by 33 productive events.

ADD per-run cancellation (AbortSignal or a returned handle). killAll() (src/harness.ts:88) is all-or-nothing, so a soft stop of one lane reaps every student. The budget path only works because it kills from inside its own closure (src/cliStudent.ts:402).

ADD `preflight()` / `version()` to the interface. src/claudeBin.ts:17-20 deliberately refuses to spawn --version and hands the question to a preflight that only knows about `claude`; a Codex/Cursor adapter has no way to say 'my binary resolved but is the wrong major version'.

WIRE warm sessions into the board loop, or stop claiming them. Protector.attach exists (protector.ts:143-148) and is never passed (live.ts:206). Until a WarmCliSession per pool slot backs each dispatch, every measurement in #301 compares a cold claude-code lane against a cold second lane, and the engine's headline saving is untested in production. This is arguably the single highest-value change in the layer.

For a Codex adapter specifically, the concrete blockers are, in order: (1) `claudeBin` in the shared options (src/harness.ts:76) with no per-harness bin config; (2) no effort field, so `-c model_reasoning_effort` is unreachable; (3) permissionMode is a free string whose only special value is Claude's (src/cliStudent.ts:283), with no sandbox axis; (4) `isInfraFailure` is not a harness member (live.ts:2129), so Codex's crash wording must impersonate Claude's; (5) session ids in Codex are rollout-file based, i.e. adopt-only like OpenCode — 6ffdbbc already solved that half; (6) no transcript member, though Codex emits a JSONL event stream that would map cleanly onto one.
open_questions: Does the installed `claude` CLI actually accept `--tools <A> <B> ...` as a space-separated list? The flag is emitted unconditionally (src/cliStudent.ts:302) and the measured -11,382 tok/turn saving depends on it, but nothing in this repo verifies it against a real binary — every test uses a faked spawn (test/studentTools.test.ts:32-43). If the flag were renamed or removed upstream, students would silently run the full surface (or fail to spawn) with no signal.

Is `--verbose` still required with `-p --output-format stream-json`? The comment at src/cliStudent.ts:297 asserts it is. If that changed, the single-blob fallback (src/cliStudent.ts:458-460) would mask it and per-message usage would silently vanish, taking the budget and the live grid with it.

Does the CLI expose any quota/usage-left surface (a `/usage`-style command, a rate-limit header, an env-readable plan state) that a `quotaLeft()` could call? Nothing in the repo reads one, and the answer determines whether the proposed member is implementable for claude-code or must stay `capabilities.quota: false`.

Which Codex CLI version is the target, and does it support a caller-named session/rollout id? If `codex exec resume --last` / `resume <id>` is the only handle, the adapter is adopt-only (seedableSessions: false) exactly like OpenCode — already supported by 6ffdbbc — but if rollout files can be seeded, the seed path applies instead. The distinction decides whether the first run of every slot pays cold ramp-up.

Is the OpenCode `step-finish` `input` field cumulative-per-step or per-step-delta on MULTI-step runs? addStepTokens sums it across steps (src/openCodeHarness.ts:111) and test/openCodeHarness.test.ts:64-71 asserts 100+200=300, but the arithmetic was only verified on a SINGLE-step run (input 6472 + output 2 + cache.read 5 == total 6479). If `input` is cumulative context rather than fresh tokens, every multi-step OpenCode row over-reports input — the direction that would wrongly condemn the lane in #301.

Should the budget/idle watchdog become a generic wrapper around any adapter's event stream, or stay per-adapter? A wrapper closes OpenCode's missing-watchdog gap for free but requires a uniform mid-run usage event, which `capabilities.streamsUsage` would have to gate. Which way v2 goes changes whether `budgetStop` remains a capability at all.

What is the intended relationship between `WarmCliSession` and `Protector`? The `attach` hook (protector.ts:146) implies one session object per worker, but no call site wires it and no test covers the combination. Is the v2 plan one warm slot per Protector worker, or per (repo, tier, role) as the assignment ladder at protector.ts:206-223 would suggest?

Does anything consume `~/.claude-study-room/usage.jsonl` yet? README.md:194-199 says cost_extract.py / comparator.py / ratio.py 'should read this file instead' — is that migration done, or is the $2.72/AC baseline still produced by transcript walking with the hardcoded path at audit-correlate.ts:12? #301's first AC ('a comparison script reads the usage store') suggests not.

Is there an existing rule for which lane a task is routed to once #300 lands — 'trivial and mechanical only' is stated in the issue body, but `tierForDifficulty()`/`effectiveDifficulty()` currently returns a Tier only. Does the routing key on difficulty label, AC count (src/config.ts acTiering), or an explicit per-repo config map?
